_comment: Template for wiring up a new TTS backend without touching tts_adapter.py. Copy this file, fill in the real values, and pick it under Models & voice > Adapter (or point TTS_ADAPTER_CONFIG at it).
_comment_voices: Where this backend LISTS its voices. Optional; defaults to OpenAI's /v1/audio/voices. The reply may be ["name", ...], {"data":[{"id":...}]}, {"voices":[...]} or a map of id -> details — all four are read. Getting this wrong is quiet rather than loud: an unreadable list means 'could not find out', so the panel falls back to stock OpenAI names and the check that stops a call asking for a voice this backend does not have simply never runs.
_comment_static: Sent on every request as-is. Put the audio format field here (response_format, format, output_format — whatever this backend calls it): the Test voice button varies it to ask for wav, which is how it measures the real sample rate.
_comment_audio: sample_rate MUST match what the backend actually produces. It is a label attached to the samples, not something carried in them, so a wrong value plays at the wrong speed and pitch and NOTHING reports an error — declare half the real rate and the DJ drags an octave low. It is also host-dependent on some engines (a GPU box and a CPU box can differ by 2x), so check it on the machine you deploy to. Press Test voice: it reads the rate out of the backend's own wav header and tells you if this number disagrees.
